The Incident Between Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), Suhayb (RA) and Bilaal (RA) with Regard to Abu Sufyaan (RA)

Hadhrat Aa'idh bin Umar narrates that Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) (who was not yet a Muslim) once approached a gathering that included Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) and Hadhrat Bilaal (RA). They passed a remark saying, "The swords of Allaah had not yet taken the necks of Allaah's enemies as they ought to have." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said to them, "Are you addressing those words to the elder of the Quraysh and their leader?" When he then reported the matter to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Abu Bakr! You may have made them angry and if you did make them angry, you would have angered your Rabb as well." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then went back to them and asked, "Dear brothers! Have I made you angry?" They graciously replied, "Not at all. May Allaah forgive you, dear brother."[^2]

Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was once passing by with a prisoner for whom he had sought amnesty from Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) who was sitting in the Masjid asked, "Who is this man with you?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "He is my Mushrik prisoner for whom I have sought amnesty from Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) commented, "His neck would have been a perfect place for a sword to strike." This infuriated Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Seeing Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) angry, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "Why do I see you so angry?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "When I passed by Suhayb with this prisoner, he remarked, 'His neck would have been a perfect place for a sword to strike.'" "Have you not perhaps hurt him?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) swore by Allaah that he had not, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Had you hurt him, you would have hurt Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ as well."[^3]
